name: ANTIGUA
lead: Antigua and Barbuda is a tiny twin-island nation in the eastern Caribbean. Antigua has about 365 beaches, one for every day of the year. Quiet Barbuda has the Caribbean's largest frigatebird colony. Coral reefs, a Georgian naval dockyard, and turquoise water fit into just 440 km².
geo: Antigua is a low, flat limestone island ringed by coral reefs. The volcanic southwest rises to Mount Obama at 402 m, the only real peak.
Barbuda lies 50 km north. It is even flatter and wilder, with scrub, pink-tinged sand, and a vast lagoon. Redonda, the third island, is an uninhabited rocky cliff.
animals: The magnificent frigatebird is the national bird. Males puff up a scarlet throat pouch the size of a balloon. Thousands gather at Barbuda's Codrington Lagoon each autumn.
European settlers brought fallow deer 400 years ago. They still roam Barbuda's scrubland. Coral reefs teem with over 170 fish species.
culture: Carnival erupts every late July and August. It marks the end of slavery in 1834. Streets fill with feathered costumes, soca music, and calypso contests.
Cricket is almost a religion here, and the nation has produced world-class players. Pepperpot stew and fungee (cornmeal with okra) link tables to African roots.
history: Siboney people arrived around 2400 BC, then Arawak and Carib. Columbus spotted Antigua in 1493. Britain took over in 1632, planting sugar cane and bringing enslaved Africans. Their descendants are about 96% of the people today.
Slavery ended on 1 August 1834. Independence came on 1 November 1981, with Vere Bird as first prime minister.
wows: You could visit a different beach every day of the year.
Nelson's Dockyard is the only working Georgian naval dockyard in the world.
The highest peak was renamed Mount Obama in 2009.
Crushed red coral and shells tint Barbuda's sand pink.
One US dollar has bought 2.70 XCD since 1976.
The country joined the United Nations in 1981, the year of independence.
Male frigatebirds can stay airborne for weeks, napping while they glide.

myths.myth: Frigatebirds dive and swim for fish
myths.fact: They never land on water. Their feathers are not waterproof. They snatch fish at the surface.
